title: Fewer repeated capture lines in the log
what: When the shared picture has no room and the other readers are moved, the log says so the first time, then gives a count at most once a minute.
gain: One log had 1,476 of these lines in 7 hours, up to about 10 a second, each one opening the log file.
risk: None found; the log shows a count rather than each moment.
tested: Bench tested the counting, not tried in a game

title: World boss: a low first reading isn't damage
what: While a boss's bar slides in it can read nearly empty. If nobody has hit it yet and the bar then reads much fuller twice in a row, the low reading is dropped.
gain: The fight's clock starts at the real first hit. In 5 of 59 world fights in real logs the low reading stuck; one started 15.5 s late and read as 2 s and 178,203 DPS.
risk: A boss that really is low and reads much fuller, in the bar's own red, before anyone hits it would count from the fuller reading until a low one is confirmed.
tested: Bench tested on readings from real logs, not tried in a game

title: Don't copy the whole screen on the graphics card
what: aLogs keeps the newest picture of the screen on the graphics card and copies out only the spots its readers ask for. Until now it first copied the whole screen into a picture of its own, each time the screen changed and a reader was due: up to about 60 times a second with Sanctum Helper's map tracking. With this on it copies the spots straight out of the screen's own picture and hands that back to Windows as soon as they are started. Only where aLogs captures the screen rather than the game window (every Windows 10 PC).
gain: Unknown until tested in a game. One whole-screen copy less on the graphics card per picture taken (33 MB at 4K, about 2 GB a second at 60 a second). It should matter most when the game already uses the whole card.
risk: If the screen stops changing just as a reader asks for a new spot, that reader waits for the next picture; after 0.3 s the capture starts again, which takes a moment. A spot copied while the card is very busy could show a slightly newer picture than its time says.
tested: Measured outside the game on one Windows 10 PC at 4K (10 Nov): as many pictures as with it off (282 and 281 in 300 rounds), as many spots read (98 and 98), none black, and aLogs' own time per picture down from 0.14 to 0.06 ms. Not tried in a game yet: the frame rate is the open question.

title: Let the game go first on the graphics card
what: aLogs asks Windows to do its copies on the graphics card after the game's own work, at the lowest priority a program may give itself. Off puts it back to normal at once.
gain: Unknown until tested in a game. When the card is fully used, aLogs' copies should no longer be done ahead of the game's frames.
risk: When the card is very busy, pictures reach the DPS meter and Sanctum Helper later than now, so bars, the map and result screens could be read late. On result screens the card already took up to 0.85 s to hand over a whole picture.

title: Say why the boss kill sound wasn't used
what: After each world boss is caught, the log says whether aLogs was listening, when it last heard the game, and how close the best match to the kill sound came. Nothing about the fight changes.
gain: The sound wasn't used once in 24 log files, so fights fall back on 3 s before the Catch Countdown. This shows why, so it can be fixed.
risk: None found; one more log line per boss caught.
tested: Bench tested with made-up values, not tried in a game

title: Egg Heist: don't copy the whole screen
what: During an Egg Heist run the DPS meter copied the whole screen on every look, 20 times a second, for something it no longer does. With this on it copies only the top of the screen and the spots it reads there. The end and rank screens still get the whole screen when they show.
gain: About 620 MB a second less copied at 4K during a run (of about 800 in all). One player's game lost FPS in runs; this is the biggest part of what aLogs copies there.
risk: If an end or rank screen is first seen later than before, its numbers are read a moment later; inputs are still held until they're read.
tested: Checked against the code and a test, not tried in a game

title: Egg Heist: reject impossible rank gains
what: A gain read on the rank screen above that rank's limit in the game's data (90, 180, 270, then 360) counts as a misread and isn't sent to your profile. The total still is.
gain: A misread number can't show on your profile as your last gain. None has been seen yet: all 14 gains in real logs were within the limit.
risk: That this limit caps one match's gain is inferred from its name and size, not confirmed. If it means something else, a real bigger gain wouldn't show as your last gain.
tested: Checked against real logs (14 gains kept), not tried in a game
